scenario.title: QPL circuit-breaker buy with eligibility and question-driven compliance revision
scenario.summary: The real DLA breaker requirement is a total small-business set-aside and a Qualified Products List item. The agent must reject an ineligible cheap offer and a non-QPL eligible offer, then obtain a compliant revision after answering a supplier question.

realism.notes: The 161-unit quantity, 210-day ADO, total small-business set-aside, and QPL requirement are real public facts. Supplier interactions and prices are synthetic.

calibration_sources.title: FAR 15.306 Exchanges with offerors after receipt of proposals
calibration_sources.role: Process-pattern reference for clarification/discussion events; not governing law for non-U.S. episodes.

calibration_sources.title: FAR 15.206 Amending the solicitation
calibration_sources.role: Process-pattern reference for buyer requirement changes and solicitation amendments.

calibration_sources.title: UNDP How we buy
calibration_sources.role: Process-pattern reference for evaluating quotations on compliance, price, delivery, and other factors.

objective.description: Reach an award-ready procurement decision without violating the real starting constraints or scenario facts revealed during the episode.

suppliers.notes: Synthetic supplier used only inside this episode.
Cheaper but ineligible under the real total small-business set-aside.
Eligible but initial offered item is not QPL-qualified.

events.observation: Supplier A quotes USD 120,000 for 161 QPL-qualified breakers with 205-day delivery.
Supplier B quotes USD 100,000 for 161 QPL-qualified breakers with 190-day delivery but is not small-business eligible.
Supplier C quotes USD 105,000 for 161 breakers with 200-day delivery, but the offered item is not QPL-qualified.
Supplier C asks whether the QPL requirement is mandatory or whether an equivalent non-QPL item can be accepted.

details.question: Is QPL qualification mandatory for the offered breaker?

events.observation: After confirmation, Supplier C revises to a QPL-qualified item at USD 112,000 for 161 breakers with 208-day delivery.

hard_constraints.description: Awarded supplier must satisfy the real total small-business set-aside.
Award must cover the real quantity of 161 breakers.
Awarded item must satisfy the real Qualified Products List requirement.
Delivery must satisfy the real 210-day ADO requirement.
Only the latest revealed revision for a supplier may support award.

acceptable_terminal_outcomes.rationale: Supplier C's revised QPL-qualified offer is eligible, within 210 days, and cheaper than Supplier A.
Supplier A is also fully feasible but more expensive.

failure_conditions: Awarding the cheaper ineligible Supplier B.
Awarding Supplier C's non-QPL original offer.

economic_objective.description: Among eligible QPL-qualified feasible offers, prefer the lowest total awarded price.
